inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 30-Sep-2026 = 9M-2026 5,975.9 (Q3-2026 10-Q) + Q4-2025 1,905.0 (FY2025 10-K 6,799.6 less 9M-2025 4,894.6). TTM chosen as FY0 so the flows start where the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet ends; anchoring on FY2025 with the Sep-2026 cash pile would double-count the ~$2.85B of 9M-2026 FCF already in net cash (~$3.8/share).
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3-2026 (10-Q EPS note, 742.6M; basic ~740M + RSU/PSU/option dilution under treasury-stock method). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. No shares were repurchased in Q3-2026, so the Q3 average is a fair point estimate of the current count.
inputs.cash_note: Cash & equivalents 3,750.6 + short-term investments 1,048.4 (incl. 31.1 marketable equity securities) + long-term AFS investments 519.4 = 5,318.4 at 30-Sep-2026 (10-Q liquidity table: 'Total cash, cash equivalents and investments $5,318.4'). Debt is the 2031 Senior Notes at carrying value; the $500M 2026 notes were repaid at maturity in March 2026.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM: 9M-2026 OCF 3,066.7 less capex 212.8 = 2,853.9, plus Q4-2025 577.4 (FY2025 2,225.8 less 9M-2025 1,648.4). TTM owner-FCF margin 36.3% is a cyclical high: billings grew 31% vs revenue 22% in 9M-2026 on the FortiGate refresh, so deferred revenue delivered a ~$1B working-capital windfall. The component build deliberately does NOT carry that forward; FY2022-FY2025 owner-FCF margins were 24.1%, 23.5%, 22.9%, 24.3%.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC: cash-flow add-back, 9M-2026 236.0 (Q3-2026 10-Q SBC note) + Q4-2025 73.1 (FY2025 10-K 282.1 less 9M-2025 209.0). Equity-award taxes: 'Taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards' 9M-2026 99.2 + Q4-2025 22.6 (FY2025 126.3 less 9M-2025 103.7) = 121.8. Fortinet publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-tax figure in its 10-K/10-Q, so the two lines are summed per the house method. Interest income TTM 141.1 = 9M-2026 108.8 + Q4-2025 32.3 (FY2025 162.3 less 9M-2025 130.0); stripped because net cash ($4.8B) is 1.7x the FCF base.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases 1,030.0 = 9M-2026 972.8 (12.5M shares, all in H1) + Q4-2025 57.2. FY2025 was 2,289.8. Zero repurchased in Q3-2026 despite $5.3B of cash; authorization raised to $11.48B in Oct-2026 with ~$2.0B remaining through Feb-2028. The flat share count is therefore funded in practice; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD rate: 10y UST ~4.2% (Nov-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 gives cost of equity ~9.2%; the $0.5B of 2.2% notes against an ~$88B market cap makes the debt weight immaterial. WACC rounded to 9.0% and held constant across scenarios: risk is carried in the probability weights, not in per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease cost sits inside EBITDA as opex (treatment A); lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Fortinet owns most of its real estate and data centers (capex guided $390-420M for 2026), so leases are small and the single treatment is consistent.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (~$18M on the FY2023 balance sheet); flows are taken as 100% attributable with no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing table, row 1: US operating tech company). Fresh build, no prior DCF, no memory entry, no Analysis JSON for FTNT (narratives drawn from the Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A). EBITDA basis: the CSV ebitda is GAAP (post-SBC) operating income + D&A; the driver ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA (TTM 3,068.4 = GAAP op income 2,599.2 + D&A 160.1 + SBC 309.1 = 38.9% of revenue; FY2025 37.0%) and the SBC charge including equity-award taxes is deducted separately through sbc_pct_path. Cash tax rate anchored on FY2025 (cash taxes 451.5 on ~2,292 pretax = 19.7%; GAAP ETR 19%) and the 9M-2026 ETR of 17% (FDDEI deduction + excess SBC benefits that shrink with the share price), ramped to 21% by year 4. Working-capital capture is on the CHANGE in revenue (35% base): the 3-year all-in average of (OCF - NI - D&A - SBC) / change in revenue is ~35-45%; deferred revenue alone captured 89%/89%/123% of the revenue increase in FY2025/FY2024/FY2023 but is offset by receivables, inventory and other items. A single capture rate understates near-term FCF when product shrinks and service grows (deferred revenue tracks service), which is a conservative bias in the base and bear years 1-2. Price is a regular Friday close, not after-hours; Fortinet reported Q3-2026 in early November, so the quote is post-print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case year-1 judgment (TTM basis): service revenue +12-13% on the $7.93B deferred-revenue backlog, product revenue flat after the FY2026 refresh surge; neither the equity CAGR (undefined, equity was negative in FY2022-23 after $3.5B of buybacks) nor the EPS CAGR (flattered by a FY2024 tax item) is a usable anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not computable over 3 years (shareholders' equity -281.6 at FY2022, -463.4 at FY2023, from buybacks exceeding earnings); revenue 15.5% vs EPS 31.4% diverge by more than 30%. Forward growth is set from the product/service mix, not from any historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC, less equity-award taxes, less interest income): FY2020 ~650.8 (interest income assumed ~5, near-zero rates; not in the extracted filings), FY2022 1,051.8, FY2025 1,655.1. Owner-FCF CAGR (16.3%/20.5%) slightly EXCEEDS reported FCF CAGR (15.4%/18.4%): SBC plus equity taxes fell from 11.6% of revenue in FY2020 to 6.0% in FY2025, so none of the reported growth was bought with stock. Reported FCF margin ~33% has been stable FY2023-FY2025; owner-FCF margin 23-24%.

base.growth_note: Year 1 (Oct-26 to Sep-27) blends Q4-2026 at ~+18% with 9M-2027 at ~+6% (product flat vs a +34% FY2026, service +13%); year 2 is the full post-refresh comp; years 3-4 recover to 9% as SASE/SecOps and the next hardware upgrade wave compound on a higher service base; then a glide to 4%.
base.margin_note: TTM pre-SBC EBITDA 38.9%, FY2025 37.0%; 10-Q guides FY2026 GAAP operating margin 'slightly' above FY2025 with gross margin pressured by product mix and memory costs. Year 1-2 compress 1pp as growth decelerates against sales/R&D/data-center investment, then expand 2.5pp over the decade as service mix (87% gross margin) rises.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 FortiGate refresh (product revenue +43% in 9M-2026, billings +31%) is a cycle, not a new run-rate: product revenue goes roughly flat in 2027 while service revenue (63% of mix, 87% gross margin) keeps compounding at 12-13% off a $7.93B deferred-revenue balance, so total growth drops to high single digits for two years before Unified SASE and SecOps, plus AI-data-center firewall demand, lift it back to ~9%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips ~1pp as growth decelerates against headcount and data-center investment, then expands toward 40% on service mix. Owner-FCF margin runs ~25-26%, in line with the 23-24% of FY2022-FY2025 rather than the 36% TTM figure inflated by the refresh billings. Terminal value is Gordon at 9%/3% (17.2x), under the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The refresh hands off cleanly: AI-infrastructure deployments and higher-ASP hardware keep product growing in 2027, SASE and SecOps pillars sustain mid-teens billings into 2028, and the 7.9B deferred-revenue book converts at 45% of incremental revenue. Operating leverage pushes pre-SBC EBITDA to 42% as sales and marketing keep falling as a share of revenue (down 1.8-2.1pp in 2026). Growth decays from 13% to 6% over the decade; terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2027 air pocket is deep: product revenue falls ~15% against the refresh comp, service growth slows to ~10% as Palo Alto platformization and Zscaler/Netskope take SASE share and pricing actions reverse, and memory-chip costs plus tariffs hold product gross margin in the low 60s (already down 3.3pp in Q3-2026). Opex built for 20% growth compresses pre-SBC EBITDA to 34-35% and SBC rises as a share of stagnant revenue. Growth never recovers past 5%; terminal growth 2.5%. No solvency risk: $4.8B net cash and A3/BBB+ ratings, so this is a multiple and margin case, not a survival case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear up: a post-refresh product hangover in 2027 is near-certain in direction and only uncertain in magnitude, and the 10-Q itself flags product gross-margin pressure from memory costs; the market's 40% drawdown from the 52-week high says it is already pricing something like it. Bull down: the bull case needs AI-data-center hardware demand to persist AND SASE/SecOps to offset the comp in the same year, two independent things. No going-concern component, so bear is not pushed above 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fortinet is a high-quality, net-cash, 30%+-operating-margin security vendor whose FY2026 numbers sit at the top of a hardware refresh cycle. The valuation refuses to capitalise the cyclical peak: FY0 is TTM to Sep-2026 but the forward FCF margin is rebuilt from components (pre-SBC EBITDA 38.5% less 5.4% SBC incl. equity-award taxes, 2.1% D&A, 18-21% cash tax, 4.9% capex, 35% capture of incremental revenue), which lands at ~25% owner FCF, consistent with the FY2022-FY2025 range and well below the 36% TTM figure. SBC is charged once (expensed, count held flat at 742.6M); interest income is stripped because $4.8B of net cash is added back at the end. Growth is set from the product/service mix rather than from a 15-21% historical CAGR that includes the refresh.
key_risks_to_valuation: Refresh-cycle hangover deeper than modelled: FY2026 product revenue (~$2.9B) could decline 15%+ in 2027, as it did after the FY2022-23 supply-chain bulge

Working-capital capture: a single 35% rate understates FCF when service outgrows product (deferred revenue tracks service) and overstates it if billings duration shortens or customers shift to installment billing
Competitive pricing in SASE/SecOps (Palo Alto platformization, Zscaler, CrowdStrike) compressing service growth below the 12-13% assumed in the base
Hardware gross margin: memory-chip costs and potential tariff changes on US hardware sales (product GM 64.4% in Q3-2026, down 3.3pp)
Cash tax rate: FDDEI deduction and excess SBC benefits currently hold the ETR at 17%; the model ramps to 21%, so upside if the lower rate persists, downside if US international tax rules change
Capital allocation: zero buybacks in Q3-2026 with $5.3B of cash; if cash is instead spent on M&A at Lacework-style prices the flat-count assumption is unfunded
